page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 48 dedicated AWS Graviton3 physical cores using the ARM64 architecture running at 2.6 GHz. It features 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance is equipped with 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. Memory performance is a key strength, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top 10 percent tier, supported by uncached read bandwidth of 274.85 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, software compilation, and Redis SET operations, which reached 76.38 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, remain in the average tier.

The c7gd.12xlarge exhibits a performance tradeoff in LLM text generation; while text generation with a medium 7B model is strong, text generation with a small 135M model falls into the bottom 25 percent tier. Given the combination of dedicated ARM cores, high memory bandwidth, and local NVMe SSD storage, this instance is designed for multi-threaded compute workloads, database hosting, software compilation pipelines, and high-throughput web serving. The custom ARM architecture offers resource density and power efficiency advantages over traditional x86 hardware, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated ARM64 physical cores powered by AWS Graviton3 processors running at 2.6 GHz. It is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network speed of 22 Gbps. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers top-tier memory performance, ranking in the top 10 percent of Passmark memory benchmarks, alongside strong multi-core CPU and database execution capabilities. Single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation represent relative performance bottlenecks, landing in the average and weak tiers respectively. Lacking x86 vector extensions, the c7gd.12xlarge is designed for multi-threaded workloads, high-throughput database operations, software compilation, and static web serving where local high-speed storage and ARM-based resource density provide qualitative cost-efficiency advantages.
